GUIDES.title: How to choose a padel racket
GUIDES.seoTitle: How to choose a padel racket
GUIDES.description: Pick the padel racket shape first, then the feel. Beginners: round, soft and light. Intermediate: try a teardrop. Sore arm: comfort first.
GUIDES.tldrLead: Pick the shape first, then the feel. Most players are happier with a racket that is easier than they think they need.
tldr: Beginners: round shape, soft core, lighter weight.
Intermediate: try a teardrop for more all-round play.
Sore arm: comfort first, power can come later.

steps.title: Shape: round, teardrop or diamond
steps.body: Round rackets have the sweet spot low and central, so they forgive mishits. Teardrop is the all-rounder. Diamond puts weight at the top for big smashes, but punishes late hits.

steps.title: Feel: soft, medium or hard
steps.body: A soft core is comfortable and gives easy depth from the back. A hard core gives more control and pop at the net, but needs more effort and is harder on the arm.

steps.title: Weight: lighter is often better
steps.body: Most rackets weigh 345 to 375 g. Lighter rackets are quicker at the net and easier on the arm over a long match. Heavier ones add power but tire you faster.

steps.title: Balance: where the weight sits
steps.body: Low balance feels quick and easy to control. High balance adds power to smashes but feels slower in fast exchanges. Shape usually sets the balance for you.

steps.title: Your level, honestly
steps.body: Beginners do best with a round, soft racket. Intermediate players can try a teardrop. Diamonds suit advanced players with clean technique who attack a lot.

steps.title: Your side of the court
steps.body: Right-side players defend and build points, so control rackets fit well. Left-side players finish more points with smashes, so power rackets make more sense.

steps.title: Sore arm? Put comfort first
steps.body: If you have tennis elbow or a sore wrist, pick a soft core, low balance and a lighter weight. Add an overgrip and hold the racket loosely.

GUIDES.title: Beginner padel tips that actually help
GUIDES.seoTitle: Beginner padel tips that actually help
GUIDES.description: Beginner padel tips that help: wait for the ball off the back glass, grip loosely, keep volleys short, lob often and move with your partner.
GUIDES.tldrLead: Most new players lose points by hitting too hard and too early. Slow down, use the glass and keep the ball in play.
tldr: Wait for the ball to come off the back glass.
Grip loosely and keep volleys short.
Lob often, and move as one with your partner.

steps.title: Let the ball come off the glass
steps.body: New players rush to hit the ball before it reaches the back wall. Wait for it. The glass slows the ball down and gives you time to set up a calm return.

steps.title: Hold the racket loosely
steps.body: A tight grip tires your arm and sends blocks flying long. Squeeze only at contact, and keep your wrist firm but relaxed between shots.

steps.title: Lob more than you think
steps.body: The lob is the most useful shot in padel. A deep lob pushes the other pair back from the net and gives your team time to move forward.

steps.title: Move with your partner
steps.body: Stay side by side, like you are joined by a rope. When one moves forward or back, the other follows. Gaps between you are where points are lost.

steps.title: Keep volleys short
steps.body: At the net, think block, not swing. Hold the racket in front of you and push the ball deep with a short movement.

steps.title: Serve low and deep
steps.body: The serve is underhand and starts the point, not wins it. Aim deep towards the glass and focus on getting it in every time.

steps.title: Do not smash every high ball
steps.body: Most smashes from beginners land in the glass and bounce back as an easy ball. Use a bandeja, a controlled overhead, to keep your spot at the net.

steps.title: Start with a forgiving racket
steps.body: A round racket with a soft core and big sweet spot hides mishits while you learn. Save diamond rackets for when your technique is steady.

GUIDES.title: Round vs teardrop vs diamond
GUIDES.description: Round vs teardrop vs diamond padel rackets: round forgives and gives the most control, diamond hits hardest, teardrop sits in between.
GUIDES.tldrLead: Shape decides where the sweet spot sits and how the racket swings. Round forgives, diamond hits hardest, teardrop sits in between.
tldr: Round: big sweet spot, most control, best to learn with.
Teardrop: balanced, a good second racket for most players.
Diamond: most power, smallest sweet spot, for clean technique.

steps.title: Where the sweet spot sits
steps.body: On a round racket it sits low and central, close to your hand. On a diamond it moves up towards the tip, where the ball travels faster but is harder to find.

steps.title: How the racket swings
steps.body: Round rackets keep the weight near the handle, so they feel quick. Diamonds carry weight at the top, which adds power but feels slower at the net.

steps.title: Control from the back
steps.body: Round rackets make lobs and deep balls from the glass easier to place. Diamonds tend to send defensive shots longer than you meant.

steps.title: Power on smashes
steps.body: Diamonds win here. The weight at the top turns a good swing into a smash that reaches the fence. Teardrops give some of that with less risk.

steps.title: How forgiving it is
steps.body: Hit off centre with a round racket and the ball still goes over. With a diamond the same hit often dies in the net or flies out.

steps.title: Which one to buy
steps.body: Learning or defending: round. Playing a bit of everything: teardrop. Attacking from the left with solid technique: diamond.

GUIDES.title: Right side or left side?
GUIDES.description: Right or left side in padel? The right side builds the point, the left finishes it with overheads. Pick the side that suits how you play.
GUIDES.tldrLead: The right side builds the point and the left side finishes it. Pick the side that suits how you like to play, not just your forehand.
tldr: Right side: steady, patient, plays most balls from the middle.
Left side: takes the overheads and finishes points.
Right-handers on the left get the forehand in the middle.

steps.title: What the right side does
steps.body: The right player keeps rallies going, returns deep and sets up the point. Patience and consistency matter more than power here.

steps.title: What the left side does
steps.body: The left player takes most overheads and smashes, and is expected to finish points. It needs confidence and a strong overhead.

steps.title: Who takes the middle
steps.body: With two right-handers, the left player has the forehand in the middle, so they take most balls there. Agree on this before the match.

steps.title: Left-handers
steps.body: A left-hander often plays the right side, so both forehands cover the middle. It can also work on the left for players with a big overhead.

steps.title: Your racket for each side
steps.body: Right-side players usually prefer a control racket for steady returns. Left-side players often pick a teardrop or diamond for more smash power.

steps.title: Try both
steps.body: Play a few weeks on each side before you decide. Many players find their side surprises them, especially if they came from tennis.

GUIDES.title: Rackets for tennis elbow
GUIDES.description: Padel rackets for tennis elbow: a soft core, low balance and lighter weight. Hold it loosely, add an overgrip and see a physio if pain lasts.
GUIDES.tldrLead: A soft, light racket with low balance takes most of the shock away from your arm. How you hold it matters just as much.
tldr: Pick a soft core, low balance and a lighter weight.
Hold the racket loosely and use an overgrip.
See a physio if the pain lasts more than a few weeks.
GUIDES.stepsTitle: 6 things that help a sore arm

steps.title: Go for a soft core
steps.body: Soft EVA or foam cores take in more of the shock at contact. Hard cores send more vibration into your elbow on every hit.

steps.title: Keep the weight low
steps.body: A lighter racket is easier to swing late in a match, when tired muscles let more strain reach the elbow. Look at 345 to 360 g.

steps.title: Choose low balance
steps.body: Weight near the handle means less leverage on your forearm. Round rackets usually have the lowest balance.

steps.title: Hold it loosely
steps.body: Gripping hard is one of the main causes of elbow pain. Squeeze only at contact and relax between shots.

steps.title: Add an overgrip
steps.body: A thicker, softer grip means you do not have to squeeze as hard. One or two overgrips is enough for most hands.

steps.title: Rest and see a physio
steps.body: If the pain lasts more than a few weeks, take a break and get it checked. A racket helps, but it does not replace treatment.

INFO.title: About PadelRecs
INFO.description: PadelRecs is a free, ad-light side project where padel players share what they really think of their rackets. Brands cannot pay to be listed.
intro: A free, ad-light side project where padel players share what they really think of their rackets. Built and kept by padel players.

sections.title: What this is
body: PadelRecs collects what real players think of their rackets. Votes and reviews left on the site, plus summaries of Reddit threads, forum posts, YouTube reviews and blogs.
Every racket gets one player score, so you can see at a glance what people actually think.

sections.title: Who runs it
body: Kept by padel players who got tired of racket reviews that read like adverts. It started as a spreadsheet of what friends said about their rackets.

sections.title: How it stays honest
body: Brands cannot pay to be listed, ranked or reviewed. Scores come only from players, and every review on the site is checked by a real person before it counts.
If a racket is bad, the score says so.

sections.title: How it pays for itself
body: Some links to shops are affiliate links. If you buy through one, the shop pays a small commission. It never changes a score or a ranking.

sections.title: How the score works
body: One number from 0 to 100, built from votes and reviews here and from around the web.

sayHi.title: Say hi
sayHi.body: Spotted a mistake, want a racket added, or just want to talk padel? Email {contactLink}. A real person reads every message.

INFO.title: How the score works
INFO.description: Every padel racket on PadelRecs gets one player score from 0 to 100, built only from what players say, here and around the web. Brands cannot buy it.
intro: Every racket gets one player score from 0 to 100. It comes only from what players say, here and around the web. Brands cannot buy it.

sections.title: Where the opinions come from
body: Reviews left on PadelRecs, plus Reddit threads, padel forums, YouTube reviews and blog posts about each racket.

sections.title: Web reviews are read and summarised
body: Each video, thread and post is summarised and read as loved it, mixed or not for them. Posts without a clear verdict still show, but do not move the score.

sections.title: Turned into one number
body: Loved it counts for the racket, mixed counts a little against it and not for me counts more.
Volume matters too: a racket with many reviews can reach the high 80s and 90s. With only a few, the score stays modest until more players weigh in.

sections.title: What the colours mean
body: Green means 85 or more: players love it. Yellow means 70 to 84: good, with some trade-offs. White means under 70: mixed opinions.

sections.title: When a score shows
body: A racket needs at least 5 reviews with a clear verdict before it gets a score. Until then it shows "Not enough votes yet".

sections.title: It keeps updating
body: New reviews change the score as they come in, so rackets can move up or down over time. Quick votes on racket pages show beside the score, not inside it.

INFO.title: Affiliate disclosure
INFO.description: Some PadelRecs links to shops earn a small commission. It costs nothing extra and never changes a score, a ranking or a review.
intro: Some links to shops earn a small commission. It costs you nothing extra and never changes a score, a ranking or a review.

sections.title: What an affiliate link is
body: A link to a shop that tells the shop you came from PadelRecs. If you buy something, the shop pays a small commission.

sections.title: Which links are affiliate links
body: Only "check price" links that go to shops, including Amazon. Links to Reddit, YouTube, blogs and other pages on PadelRecs are never affiliate links.

sections.title: What it never changes
body: Scores, rankings and reviews come only from players. A racket that earns more does not rank higher, and brands cannot pay to be listed.

sections.title: Where the money goes
body: It pays for hosting and the time spent reading and summarising reviews. It keeps the site free and ad-light.

sections.title: Questions
body: If something looks off, or you think a link is not marked clearly, get in touch.
